correctness.rationale: Each six-agent profile lies in the explicit 6^6 finite universe, and each of its six perfect matchings is stable exactly when no unassigned mutually preferred pair exists. All rank comparisons and inversion weights therefore give exact polynomial coefficient counts. A separate from-scratch Python enumeration tested all 46656 profiles, giving counts N=1/2/3 of 34080/11484/1092 and 10054 profiles with stable identity. Rational identities checked symbolically; derivative numerators factor phi(1-phi) or phi^4(1-phi) with positive-coefficient polynomials for multiplicity, and -(1-phi) times positive polynomial for assortativity, establishing strict signs throughout 0<phi<1. No infinite-market inference.

value.rationale: The 3x3 market is the first size allowing three stable matchings; exact rare-event exponents 1,2,5 separate three relevant economic phenomena under increasing preference noise. This finite parameter-exact law is not interchangeable with uniform count or n-to-infinity asymptotics; it offers a useful exact benchmark for correlated-market models.
